svg.aria-label: Four stages. 1, normal operation: the messaging grid sends requests to three processing units; unit 1 holds the primary of A and a backup of C, unit 2 the primary of B and a backup of A, unit 3 the primary of C and a backup of B, and each primary replicates to its backup. 2, primary failure: unit 1 becomes unavailable and requests to it fail. 3, failover to backup: the backup of A on unit 2 is promoted to primary and the messaging grid sends requests for A to unit 2. 4, recovery: the grid creates a new backup of A on unit 3 and a new backup of C on unit 2, restoring the redundancy level
svg.text: Failure handling: primary and backup processing units
When a unit fails, the backups of its partitions are promoted and new backups are created elsewhere.
Each partition's primary handles its requests;
its backup sits on a different processing unit.
Unit 1, which holds the primary of A,
The backup of A on unit 2 is promoted, and
the messaging grid sends requests for A to it.
The grid creates new backups on other units
